raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

---

My 12 mu splits up pretty much the way it always has: about 7 mu for cotton on the field out west, and 5 mu for the wheat-maize rotation on the plot closer to the road. Cotton is where the real cash comes from around here — the maize and wheat mostly keep the family in grain and bring in a little when prices are decent. I've done it this way for most of the last ten years and I don't see a reason to shake it up.

The wheat is already in the ground — I put it down last October, the usual variety the seed shop in the township stocks. Right now it's coming out of winter. I'll watch for greening-up, and around jointing I'll topdress urea — maybe 10 kg per mu on top of what went in at planting. If the ground is dry I'll irrigate first and then put the urea on, otherwise you just waste it. Probably three irrigations total on wheat this spring: one after greening, one at jointing, and one at grain-fill if there's no good rain. I spray once for weeds early and that's usually enough.

Cotton goes in late April, same as every year. I use the improved Bt variety — not the cheapest seed, but I've tried cheaper ones and got eaten up by bollworm, so I don't mess around with that anymore. Compound fertilizer at base, then topdress urea at squaring. Altogether maybe 16 kg N per mu. The extension guy last year said I could cut back some on N, something about efficiency, but when you see cotton going pale in July it's hard to hold back — better to spend a few extra yuan on urea than watch bolls drop. I'll spray probably 4-5 times through the summer for bollworm and aphids. Irrigate twice, once at seedling and once around boll-forming — the well is metered so I don't water for fun. Picking in September and October is the hard part. My wife and I do most of it, my daughter helps on weekends when she's home from school, and I hire a neighbor's wife for a couple weeks when it's peaking.

Maize is tight — wheat combine comes off around June 10-15, and I need maize in the ground within a week. I rent the no-till planter through the co-op, hybrid seed, compound fertilizer dropped with the seed. Topdress urea at the big-trumpet stage, maybe 8-10 kg N. One or two irrigations depending on July rain. A bit of herbicide early and that's mostly it unless armyworm shows up.

My household has four but my wife works off-farm part of the year at the factory in town, and my daughter is in high school. So family labor is really me plus some help. Off-farm income is what lets me buy decent inputs without going into debt. If the cotton price drops hard this fall I'll think about shifting some cotton area to maize next year, but for this season everything is going in the ground the same as before.
